The Survival of
the Sacred Book
Early 1700s: The Discovery
Fray Francisco Ximénez, a sympathetic
Dominican friar, discovers a transcribed
Quiché manuscript in Chichicastenanao. He
translates it into Spanish in parallel columns.
Pre-1524: Oral & Lost Text
The original histories are hidden to protect
them from the Spanish conquest of the
Quiché capital, Utatlán.
1854: The European Export
Austrian traveler Dr. Carl Scherzer finds
Ximénez's forgotten translation in a Guatemalan
university library and publishes it in Vienna.
1861: The Naming
Scholar Charles Étienne Brasseur de
Bourbourg translates the text into French and
officially names it the Popol Vuh.

The Power of
the Word
In the beginning, there was only calm,
silence, and the expanse of the sky
and sea in darkness
The Progenitors
Tepeu and Gucumatz, hidden under
green and blue feathers, conferred
with the Heart of Heaven.
The Key Insight
Creation was immediate and linguistic. When they
commanded 'Earth!', the mountains and valleys instantly
surged from the waters, covered in cypress and pine.

The Revolt of
the Tools
The destruction of the Wooden Men
was total. They were not just drowned;
the domestic world turned against them
for their lack of reverence.
The Dogs:
"You gave us no food and
hit us with sticks. Now we
will devour your faces."
The Grinding Stones:
"Every day, holi, huqui, you
tormented our faces. Now we
will grind your flesh to dust."
The Pots:
"You blackened us with soot and kept
us on the fire. Now we will burn you."
The few survivors escaped into the forests, becoming the monkeys
of today -a living reminder of the wooden generation.

The Era of Arrogance
Before the sun existed, false gods claimed dominion over the twilight earth.
Afla
Vucub-Caquix (Seven Macaw)
Claimed to be the Sun and the Moon.
His power was an illusion derived from extreme
wealth: eyes of silver, teeth of shining emeralds, and
a throne of precious metals.
The Sons of Hubris
Zipacna: The First Son. Arrogant creator of
mountains.
Cabracán: The Second Son. The great shaker and
destroyer of mountains.

The Takedown of Vucub-Caquix
Step 1: The Ambush
The Hero Twins (Hunahpú &
Ixbalanqué) wait at
Vucub-Caquix's favorite
nance tree and shoot him in
the jaw with a blowgun
Step 2: The Injury
A furious Vucub-Caquix
survives and tears off
Hun-Hunahpu's arm, taking
it home to hang over the fire.
Step 3: The Disguise
The Twins disguise
themselves as ragged, elderly
healers (Zaqui-Nim-Ac &
Zaqui-Nimá-Tzlis) offering to
cure his aching jaw.
Step 4: The Extraction
They pull out his shining
emerald teeth-the source of
his pride- and replace them
with grains of white corn.
Stripped of his wealth,
Vucub-Caquix dies.

Zipacná and the 400 Boys
The Feat: Zipacná effortlessly carries a
massive tree for 400 boys building a house.
Fearing his unnatural strength, they plot
to bury him in a deep trench.
The Deception: Zipacná survives
the collapse of the trench. He cuts
his own hair and nails, letting ants
carry them to the surface to fool
the boys into celebrating his death.
The Revenge: Once the boys are
drunkenly celebrating inside, Zipacná
collapses their new house on top of
them. They are immortalized in the sky
as the star cluster Motz (the Pleiades).

The Mountain Maker Crushed
To avenge the 400 Boys, the Twins exploit Zipacna's
voracious appetite for fish and crabs.
The Shell: Made from an empty,
heavy stone basin.
The Claws: Forged from broad,
stiff leaves collected in the forest.
The Trap
The Twins lure a starving Zipacna
to the bottom of the canyon. As
he slides under the stone shell to
eat the fake crab, Mount Meauán
collapses on top of him, turning
him to stone forever.

The Poisoned Bird
Cabracan, who shook the earth and collapsed
mountains, is the final false god. The Twins
challenge him to destroy a specific mountain,
leading him on a long hike.
The Weapon
Along the way, they hunt a bird
and roast it. But they coat it in
tizate (white earth paste).
The Downfall
When offered the delicious-
smelling bird, Cabracan devours
it. The enchanted earth instantly
binds his limbs, stripping him of
his strength. He is buried alive
by the Twins.

Synthesis: The Prerequisite of Humility
The Failed Creations
& False Gods
Failed because they lacked the
intellect to respect the Creator,
respect the Creator, or
respected only themselves.
The Cleared Earth
A blank slate ready for the
final creation -humanity.
The Cosmic Equation
The Popol Vuh presents a universe that strictly demands balance and reverence. The Hero
Twins are not just adventurers; they are cosmic janitors. They must purge the earthly realm of
hubris and false idols so humanity can inherit a world properly aligned with the Heart of Heaven.

The Descent to

Trap 1: The Steep Stairs

Trap 2: The River of Blood

Trap 3: The Crossways
Four paths lie ahead-Red, White,
Yellow, and Black.
The Fatal Error
The Black Road speaks to them, claiming to be
the correct path. It is a deception, leading them
directly into the council room of the Lords.

The Humiliation at the Council
Xibalba operates on trickery. Defeat is not just physical; it is a loss of dignity.
Trick 1: The Wooden Dummies
Trick 2: The Hot Bench
Upon entering, Hun-Hunahpú and Vucub-Hunahpú
politely greet the figures seated before them. The
Lords of Xibalba erupt in mocking laughter- they are
just carved blocks of wood.
Invited to sit and rest, the Twins take a seat on a stone
bench. It is searing hot, burning them severely while
the Lords convulse with laughter at their pain.

A Notebook N

The Impossible Test
The First Twins are thrown into the Dark
House. The guards hand them a single
pine torch and two lit cigars.
The Rule
Keep them burning all night, but return
them to us whole in the morning.
The Failure
Unable to perform magic to fake the flames,
the Twins allow the torch and cigars to burn
down. They fail the test and are immediately
sacrificed by the Lords of Xibalbá.

The Tree of Pucbal-Chah
Hun-Hunahpú's severed head is placed
in the branches of a barren tree.
The Miracle
Instantly, the dead branches
burst into life, covered in
round jícara fruits. The skull
morphs to look exactly like the
fruit, perfectly hiding itself.
The Decree
Terrified by this magic, the
Lords of Xibalbá forbid
anyone from
approaching the tree or
picking its fruit.

The Conception of the Hero Twins
ixquic, the curious daughter of the
Underworld Lord Cuchumaquic, defies
the decree and approaches the tree
The Interaction:
The skull of Hun-Hunahpú
speaks to her, warning her that
the fruits are just bone. When
she asks for one anyway, the
skull spits into her open hand
The Legacy:
"In my saliva and my spittle I have given you my descendants."
Through this miraculous act, Ixquic becomes pregnant with the next generation:
the true Hero Twins, who will one day return to finish what their fathers started.
